page: Microsoft Azure F32as_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 32 dedicated physical cores with single-threaded core execution (1 thread per core), running at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. It includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing an allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The processor architecture integrates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, along with specialized instruction set extensions including AVX-512 (f, vnni, bf16), AVX-VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance contains zero GPUs and provides no bundled local storage, requiring remote managed disks for persistent and temporary storage needs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational efficiency, highlighted by top-tier single-core CPU throughput in stress-ng and top-tier execution in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Multi-core compute performance in stress-ng and PassMark places within the top 25% of evaluated cloud systems. In memory performance, the instance registered top-tier PassMark memory scores and 215.71 GB/s in large-block uncached read bandwidth. In operational testing, it produced top-tier performance in database operations alongside strong throughput in Redis SET operations and static web serving. For lightweight machine learning workloads, prompt processing and token generation with a 135M parameter LLM achieved top-tier throughput, though performance moderates on 70B parameter models.

The absence of integrated local NVMe storage requires architectural reliance on external Azure storage volumes, introducing potential network latency for disk-bound operations. However, the dedicated core architecture eliminates hyper-threading contention, resulting in consistent compute execution and solid resource density per vCPU. The instance is suited for compute-intensive batch processing, compression pipelines, in-memory caching layers, web application tiers, and compilation workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure F32as_v7 is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 32-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 32 dedicated physical cores and 128.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a 4.0 GB memory-per-core ratio without simultaneous multithreading overhead. The instance supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and VAES, though it lacks integrated local storage and hardware GPU acceleration. Benchmark testing reflects top-tier single-core CPU results and compression speeds, paired with strong multi-core computation and memory bandwidth exceeding 215 GB/s on large uncached reads. It excels at database transactions, Redis caching operations, and static web serving, while showing reliable performance in small to medium-sized LLM inference tasks. Requiring external Azure storage volumes, F32as_v7 provides a balanced, high-frequency compute profile suited for CPU-bound batch tasks, web serving, and database services.
